statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is in the low band because every hour of this window falls inside the CME weekend halt and Friday's final session retraced rather than extending one-way; Stress stays high on unresolved rates, energy and geopolitical tension.
recommendation: Tail remains well below the block threshold, so the mapped state is EA_ON for both NQ futures and the NAS100 CFD across all 24 hours. No evidence-based danger window applies inside this window because no venue is open in any hour assessed. The first live structural test is the 22:00Z Sunday reopen, followed by Monday's ISM Services PMI, both outside this horizon.
headline: Nasdaq-100 holds a record close through the weekend halt, with Friday's completed retracement keeping Tail low and Stress high
body: Assessment made during the CME equity index futures weekend halt. Futures settled at 21:00Z on 2 October and do not reopen until 22:00Z on 4 October, roughly 21 hours after this forecast window closes, so no live NQ price path exists in any of the 24 hours assessed. Friday's final session is therefore the governing evidence, and it has been re-verified for this run. The Nasdaq-100 closed at a record 30,807.93, up 306.37 points or 1.00% from a 30,501.56 previous close, after printing an intraday all-time high of 31,017.53 and then giving back about 0.68% into the close on a day range of 30,737.07 to 31,017.53. That give-back is the decisive observation under this contract: September payrolls missed badly at +29,000 against roughly 90,000 expected, with the unemployment rate up to 4.2% and average hourly earnings soft, yet the tape produced an orderly advance that retraced rather than a no-retracement extension. Implied volatility confirmed the decay, with VIX down 1.08 points or 6.59% to 15.31 and settling at its session low on a 15.30 to 16.24 range. Cross-asset evidence conflicts rather than aligns: the 10-year yield collapsed to roughly 5.17% immediately after the labour data and then reversed to close near 5.29%, while the 30-year finished near 5.64% at its highest since 2002, even as traders cut October rate-hike odds to about 16% from roughly 64% a week earlier. The Federal Reserve H.15 release for 1 October records the 2-year at 4.78%, the 10-year at 5.24% and the 30-year at 5.61%. Energy eased but stayed expensive: WTI printed a one-month low near 88.06 after the G7 announced a coordinated 100 million-barrel IEA release over four months with a frontloaded diesel component inside 20 days, then recovered to settle about 91.41, with Brent near 100 after a 2.57% decline. The U.S. average diesel price was 6.37 dollars a gallon on Friday against a 6.52 record on 22 September. The Iran conflict remains a persistent stalemate rather than a fresh discontinuity: Hormuz crude flows recovered to roughly 9.7 million barrels per day in September, near 80% of pre-war levels, while tanker insurance costs and risk premia stay elevated. Friday's leadership was also dispersed rather than uniform, with Apple down 2.66% into a record index close. A record equity level alongside a long end at post-2002 highs is a genuine tension, and conflicting cross-asset evidence raises Stress and tempers Confidence under this contract; it does not establish the persistent one-way structure, shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements that Tail measures. With every venue shut there is no mechanism for mean-reversion failure inside the window, so Tail stays in the low band throughout, easing to 8 across the Saturday dead zone before rising to 10 and 11 in the closing hours as a near-complete weekend of unpriced information accumulates ahead of a reopen that still falls outside this horizon.

lookbackSummary: The preceding 24 hours span 2 October from 02:00Z plus the first two hours of 3 October. Published Claude assessments held Tail at 20 through the Asian and European hours, lifted it to 23-24 as the pre-payrolls advance built, and peaked at 25 and 27 in the 13:00Z and 14:00Z slots immediately after the +29,000 payrolls print, the only orange hours of the day. Tail then fell back to 22-23 across the U.S. afternoon as the move retraced, and dropped to 14, 12, 11, 9 and 9 in the final five hours once the record close was in and futures entered the weekend halt. Stress stayed high throughout in a 66-79 band and Confidence held between 83 and 89.
outlookSummary: Every hour of this window falls inside the CME weekend halt, and the 22:00Z Sunday reopen sits roughly 21 hours beyond its close, so no price path can form and Tail stays in the low band throughout. Tail eases to 8 across the Saturday dead zone and rises to 10 and then 11 in the closing hours as a near-complete weekend of unpriced information accumulates. Stress eases from 65 to a 61 trough by late Saturday morning as the payrolls catalyst resolves and the G7 oil release eases energy pressure, then firms back to 67 on the unreconciled pairing of a record equity level with a 30-year yield at post-2002 highs. Confidence declines from 82 to 76 purely because the live price-path component ages with no weekend session to replace it. The characterisation is normal while the tape is shut and turns mixed in the final six hours, where the operative feature is the conflict between a soft labour print with sharply lower hike odds and a long end holding near cycle highs. The first genuine tests are the Sunday reopen and Monday's ISM Services PMI, followed by the September FOMC minutes on Wednesday and a 30-year auction on Thursday.
